title: Regional onboarding lag and burst buffer scenarios (Q2 2026)
summary: Working capacity sheet modeling GPU onboarding lag + burst (warm pool) buffer by region. Focus: quantify runway risk when vendor lead times slip, and propose triggers for burst activation and cross-region spill policies.
assumptions: 1) Baseline demand growth = +18% month-over-month for Q2 2026 (derived from telemetry trending). 2) Typical vendor onboarding lead = 6 weeks (NA), 8 weeks (EU), 10 weeks (APAC) due to customs and rack scheduling. 3) Warm pool kept at 8-12% of committed capacity by default. 4) Spot/borrowed capacity can supply up to 15% of region demand for short bursts at 2.5x unit cost. 5) SLA requirement: <2% request rejection at 95th percentile latency target.
table_lines: Month | Region | Demand GPUs (est) | Committed GPUs | Warm pool % | Warm pool GPUs | Onboard lead (weeks) | Expected new GPUs onboarded | Available GPUs = committed+warm+onboard | Shortfall GPU | Risk level

Notes: Available GPUs computed conservatively as committed + warm pool + new onboarded that month. Shortfall = Demand - Available (negative indicates deficit). Warm pool targeted to be fully cold-to-warm within 24-36 hours; activation latency captured in risk model.
Key triggers and rules:
- Trigger A: Region utilization > 78% sustained for 72 hours -> warm pool scale +10% (immediate) AND request cross-region spill up to 10% of traffic if cross-region latency penalty < 20%.
- Trigger B: Predicted shortfall next 30 days > 5% -> open spot/borrow window (supplier marketplace) + enable reserved-burst where legal/compliance allows.

- Trigger C: Vendor lead time slip noticed (>=2 weeks) -> escalate to on-call infra ops and open contingency lane: accelerate NA->EU hardware rebalancing (if compliance allows) OR increase on-demand cloud quota requests by 20%.
Mitigations mapped to risk levels:
- Low: normal warming and scheduled onboarding. Monitor only.
- Low-Medium: proactive warm-pool increase and adjust routing weights to favor lower-latency regions for non-sensitive traffic.
- Medium: enable spot-backed instances for stateless workloads; trigger cost-budget alert to finance if cost > $0.12 / GPU-hour above baseline.
- Medium-High: mobilize vendor account team; escalate procurement and request expedited shipping. Prepare customer-rate-limit plans to avoid SLA breach.
- High: enact partial rollout freezes for non-critical releases, open emergency procurement with 48-hour gating and exec notification.
Cost delta model (text):

- Baseline unit cost (committed reserved) = $0.32 / GPU-hour. Spot/borrow cost = baseline * 2.5. Emergency rental (short-term) = baseline * 4.0. Warm pool cost = baseline * 0.45 (lower utilization but reserved overhead).
- Quick formula examples: Additional hourly burn if activating 200 spot GPUs = 200 * baseline * 2.5 = (200 * 0.32 * 2.5) = $160 / hour.
Scenario exercises (for runbook):

1) Vendor delay: EU vendor delays racks by 3 weeks in June. Impact: EU shortfall rises from -159 -> -399 in May-June window. Mitigation sequence: (a) enable spot up to 15% demand, (b) invoke cross-region spill from NA with phased traffic reroute for non-PHI customers, (c) renegotiate partial shipments and air freight for critical racks.

2) Sudden demand spike (25% above forecast for NA) for two weeks in July. Impact: NA shortfall becomes -600 GPUs if warm pool not increased. Mitigation: scale warm pool immediately + borrow 12% capacity from cloud reserved burst; open marketing communication to throttle bulk batch jobs.

3) Multi-region simultaneous lag (vendor + customs) — worst-case. Activation: emergency procurement, temporary customer throttles, prioritized model routing to smaller sequence lengths, progressively degrade non-critical features.

Appendix: quick calculations and formulas used (plain text)
- Demand growth projection: demand(t+1) = demand(t) * 1.18 (monthly).
- Warm pool GPU calculation: warm_gpus = round(committed_gpus * warm_pool_pct).

- Expected new GPUs onboarded in month approximated as: floor((weeks_left_in_month / onboarding_lead_weeks) * ordered_batch_size). For conservative modeling, we used 0.6 * theoretical onboarding capacity to account for shipping/failures.
